title: HSBC posts Q3 profit of $5.1 bln, confirms forex probe
text:
HSBC posts Q3 profit of $5.1 bln, confirms forex probe

Wednesday 25 Nov 2026

* Q3 profits $5.1 billion helped by lower costs, impairments * CEO gives positive outlook, sees broadening recovery * HSBC says has not suspended any traders in FX probe * Better capital ratios, warns of regulatory uncertainty * Shares up 2 pct

LONDON (Nov 4): HSBC reported a 10 percent rise in third quarter profits on Monday — helped by tighter cost control and fewer losses from bad loans, and confirmed it was being investigated as part of a global probe into currency market trading manipulation.

Europe's largest bank said underlying pretax profit was $5.1 billion for the three months to Sept 30 — up 30 percent on a statutory basis — with strong Hong Kong and British markets together accounting for more than half of earnings and offsetting a fall in Latin American profits.

Chief Executive Stuart Gulliver said he saw evidence of a broadening recovery in which the U.S. should continue to grow, albeit slowly, and the UK would outperform the eurozone.

"There are signs for optimism around. We've always been confident, China would have a soft landing ... which is supportive for the rest of Asia-Pacific," he told a conference call with reporters.

Gulliver also confirmed that HSBC was cooperating with Britain's Financial Conduct Authority — which is leading an investigation into the $5.3-trillion-a-day foreign exchange market, that has spread to include regulators in the United States, Asia and Switzerland. Traders from some of the world's top banks, including Barclays, Citigroup and JP Morgan, have been suspended or put on leave.

HSBC, which has vowed to instill a more responsible corporate culture, after it was fined a record $1.9 billion last year for lax anti-money laundering compliance, has not taken any action against its staff, Gulliver said.

"We haven't suspended anyone. It's at a very early stage and the names we've been given so far, don't work for us any more," he said. The bank said no-one had been fired, and added that it had been contacted in October.

Regulatory caution

Despite the mushrooming FX probe, with its echoes of the recent interest rate fixing scandal, investors focused on HSBC's improved quarterly performance and growth prospects.

HSBC led the FTSE 100 index higher, with a 2.4 percent gain by 1000 GMT, and kept the European banking index in positive territory, after a call for higher capital requirements by the Swiss finance minister over the weekend, dragged sector heavyweights UBS and Credit Suisse sharply down.

"If investors are seeking a strong and dependable bank, HSBC could be the place to look. The key metrics were, on the whole, progressive," said Richard Hunter, head of equities at Hargreaves Lansdown Stockbrokers.

The rise in HSBC's profits, in line with analysts' forecasts, was underpinned by a 4 percent dip in losses from bad loans, and a $700 million fall in operating expenses to $9.6 billion, although that was mainly due to the absence of one-off items last year..

Underlying costs were up on the year due to investments, wage inflation and regulatory costs. Revenues were flat.

HSBC said its capital position improved, with a core tier one ratio — a key measure of financial strength — of 10.6 percent under tough new rules, and a leverage ratio of 4.2 percent — above an international requirement of 3 percent.

But the bank cautioned that there was significant regulatory uncertainty on the horizon, as financial watchdogs around the world continue to refine new rules, insisting banks hold more capital, in order to shore them up against any future financial crisis.

That warning was borne out over the weekend, when Swiss Finance Minister Eveline Widmer-Schlumpf was quoted as saying, authorities there were discussing raising the leverage ratio for Swiss banks to 6-10 percent — two or three times the required ratio set out by the global Basel III accord, which is being phased in by 2019.

title: HSBC says Q2 earnings surprised but Q3, Q4 growth likely to slow down; sees this as a bigger downside risk - The Economic Times

# HSBC says Q2 earnings surprised but Q3, Q4 growth likely to slow down; sees this as a bigger downside risk
HSBC says Q2 earnings surprised but Q3, Q4 growth likely to slow down; sees this as a bigger downside risk
By
Debaroti Adhikary
, ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Nov 20, 2026, 03:04:00 PM IST
Synopsis
HSBC says Indian companies delivered their strongest earnings growth in nearly two years in Q2 FY27, with 67% beating or meeting estimates. However, growth is expected to moderate in the second half. The brokerage sees a sharper consumption slowdown triggered by inflation or El Niño as a bigger downside risk.
Agencies
As India Inc wraps up the September quarter earnings season, HSBC pointed out that around 67% of companies reported results ahead of or in line with estimates, but the second half of the ongoing financial year 2027 may see a moderation in earnings growth.
In its latest ‘India Equity Strategy’, HSBC Global Investment Research said sales of companies excluding commodities grew 17% year-on-year, while net income rose 19% in Q2, making this the strongest quarter since December 2023. Mid and small-cap companies continued to lead, with earnings growth of 30% and 32%, but the growth among large caps also accelerated and the recovery broadened across sectors, it noted.
**Earnings slowdown ahead?**
### Live Events
However, after a 16% growth in net income in the first half of the ongoing financial year 2027, HSBC noted that the consensus estimate now expects growth to moderate to 12% in the second half of the financial year FY27, taking full-year growth to 14%. “In other words, a meaningful slowdown is already built into estimates, so the risk of substantial earnings downgrades seems lower. What’s more, consensus has raised FY27 earnings 1.5 ppt since end-September, reflecting better expectations for basic materials, energy and financials. Autos have seen the largest cuts, followed by cement, chemicals and insurance,” the international brokerage said, adding that FY28 expectations have also been revised on similar lines, with consensus forecasting 16% earnings growth.
Financials, industrials, metals and energy drove much of Q2 earnings growth, while autos, staples and IT were relatively weaker, HSBC said in its report. It noted that the overall EBITDA margins contracted by 60 bps, with cement and autos leading the compression, while utilities
stood out by expanding margins. The brokerage listed out key takeaways from each of the major sectors.
**What can be a bigger downside risk than earnings slowdown?**
However, HSBC sees a sharper consumption slowdown due to either inflation or El Niño conditions as a bigger downside risk. Inflationary pressures have been increasing bets for global rate hikes. India's retail inflation surged to a two-year high of 6.09% in October, crossing the Reserve Bank of India's upper tolerance limit of 6%. This came as accelerating food prices added to concerns over persistent inflationary pressures. The sharper-than-expected rise in consumer prices has strengthened expectations of further monetary tightening, with market experts anticipating a 25 basis points repo rate hike at the RBI's upcoming December monetary policy review.
HSBC's latest review on Q2 earnings comes after the global brokerage firm earlier this month upgraded Indian equities to overweight and cut mainland China to neutral. The global bank’s call comes after a multi-year valuation reset in India, stronger domestic credit growth and a more resilient earnings backdrop. HSBC said Indian equities now offer “diversification and low volatility in Asian markets dominated by AI stocks.”

HSBC had previously maintained a neutral stance on India and an overweight rating on China. It now believes India’s valuation premium has narrowed sufficiently, while earnings growth and domestic demand remain supportive. “India’s investment case has become quite compelling relative to other markets,” HSBC said in its previous Asia equity strategy report.

# HSBC RedCoin expands into wealth with tokenised fund access

- Minimum subscription of HKD 100 (funded with RCHKD 100) 1 via HSBC HK Mobile Banking App, with potentially faster settlement 2 

Hong Kong, 19 November 2026 — HSBC RedCoin (Ticker: RCHKD), HSBC’s Hong Kong dollar-denominated stablecoin, is now available on the HSBC HK Mobile Banking App (the App). 

Eligible customers will now be able to activate their stablecoin wallet in the App and use RCHKD to access a new tokenised unit class (Class SD) 3 of the HSBC Global Money Funds – Hong Kong Dollar (the Fund) 4. Winnie Ng, Head of Wealth and Premier Solutions, Hong Kong, HSBC, said: “Tokenised funds reduce traditional market friction and enable faster settlement. By bringing HSBC RedCoin together with tokenised investments, we are creating new ways for our wealth customers to access innovative investment opportunities with a lower entry threshold and a more efficient experience. Launched in 1991, the Fund is managed by HSBC Asset Management. Its dividend distributions are separate from HSBC RedCoin, which pays no interest. 

Jasmine Hung, CEO, HSBC Asset Management, Hong Kong, said: “We are delighted to launch a tokenised unit class of our long-standing Hong Kong dollar money market fund, offering investors a new digital gateway to an established fund. The launch responds to clear customer interest in practical applications for digital assets. HSBC’s Hong Kong stablecoin study found that digital asset trading and tokenised investments were the most widely recognised use case, cited by 57 per cent of respondents. 

HSBC’s Securities Services tokenises the new unit class, while its Digital Assets Custody capability provides safekeeping services for HSBC RedCoin and the tokenised unit class (Class SD) of the Fund.

# HSBC expands credit facility for China’s low-carbon sectors to $8bn 

 17 Nov 2026 

We’ve doubled the size of our Sustainability and Transition Credit Facility to $8 billion to help businesses operating in the Chinese mainland’s low-carbon and clean energy sectors to grow and expand globally. 

As well as increasing the size of the facility, we’re broadening our financial support to international businesses operating in the Chinese mainland in these sectors, empowering them to advance their own transition efforts. 

Since its launch in May, the facility has successfully supported a diverse range of sustainable transactions across key sectors. They include: 

- A €185 million (US$204 million) financing facility for EVE Energy and Sinosure for the development of a large-scale, lithium-ion battery manufacturing plant in Hungary 
- A landmark RMB745 million (US$111 million) aviation finance and transition loan for China Eastern Airlines – our first RMB-denominated facility of its kind in Asia 
- Guarantees enabling major infrastructure development in the Middle East 

## Supporting the transition

The dedicated credit facility offers financing to eligible businesses in the transition ecosystem operating in a range of sectors, including clean power, electrification of transport, data centres and artificial intelligence. 

Through the facility, HSBC increases credit limits for eligible companies, streamlines credit approvals and develops tailored financial solutions to help bring clean technologies and solutions to markets more efficiently. 

Chaoni Huang, Asia Head of Sustainable Finance and Transition at HSBC, said: “We look forward to supporting more companies as they expand overseas and navigate their own transition in the Chinese mainland. 

“HSBC’s global reach and market expertise make us well placed to navigate this opportunity.” 

Find out more about how we’re supporting our customers and our ambition to become a net zero bank by 2050.

# Tencent says new US chip curbs won’t hurt cloud revenue, may slow model training

By

Published Nov 18, 2026, 04:28 AM

Updated Nov 18, 2026, 08:36 AM

© Reuters. FILE PHOTO: A logo of Tencent at an exhibition center during organized media tour in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China, June 11, 2026. REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov/File Photo

0700-1.23%

BEIJING, Nov 18 (Reuters) - China’s Tencent Holdings said on Wednesday that new US restrictions on remote access to advanced AI chips would not substantially hurt its cloud revenue, though they would likely slow development of its next AI model.

Washington this week unveiled rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips through overseas data centres. Shares in Chinese cloud service providers, including Tencent, fell on Tuesday after the announcement.

"We actually don’t see an impact, because our cloud business today is primarily running inference," Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell told analysts on a post-earnings call.

Mitchell said Tencent’s more efficient models could now be run on a "surprisingly limited number" of domestic chips.

"We think that our cloud revenue will not be substantially adversely affected by the changes," he said.

President Martin Lau called the tighter restrictions "unfortunate" and said they left Chinese companies with less advanced computing power.

Lau said the measures would affect AI model training and likely slow development of Tencent’s next model in the near term.

Over the longer run, Chinese companies would have to rely on domestic supply chains and chips, he said, adding that the latest restrictions were likely to accelerate their development.

MISSING EXPECTATIONS

author: Zheng Xutong
text:
Tencent’s Capex to Remain at Peak Levels Through 2027 on AI Investment

Tencent’s Capex to Remain at Peak Levels Through 2027 on AI Investment

 Zheng Xutong 

DATE: Nov 19 2026

 Tencent’s Capex to Remain at Peak Levels Through 2027 on AI Investment

(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- Tencent Holdings’ capital expenditure will remain at peak levels through next year as a result of heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure, but the Chinese internet giant anticipates an upswing in financial performance from 2028 onward, executives said on its latest earnings conference call.

Capex prepayments were unusually high in the second and third quarters of this year, Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell said on the call late yesterday, adding that as Tencent has already secured long-term contracts, cash outflows for prepayments will decline and some quarters may even see reversals.

Cash-based capex, these prepayments, has peaked and is likely to fluctuate around peak levels for the rest of this year and through 2027, before starting to decline, he noted.

Capex surged more than six times to CNY81.4 billion (USD12.2 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from a year earlier, with cash payments of CNY65.1 billion, the Shenzhen-based company’s third-quarter earnings report showed.

President Martin Lau said current infrastructure investments are mainly aimed at launching AI-native businesses, and once this infrastructure in in place, it will enable the continuous training of new-generation models and generate tokens. So when capex commitments for this year and the next are completed, Tencent will be able to use the infrastructure in 2028, leading to a marked improvement in its financial performance, he pointed out.

During Tencent’s recent annual management meeting, its leadership emphasised that if the company fails to get on board fully with the AI revolution, then it risks being disrupted and losing ground to competitors, according to the minutes posted on its social media accounts on Nov. 16. Tencent wants half of its 100,000 employees to act as an “army,” defending existing businesses, while the other half acts as a “navy,” exploring new opportunities in AI.

Equipment prices have been elevated this year and will remain so in 2027, but are expected to fall substantially in 2028, Lau said on the call, adding that in the course of AI model training and inference, computing efficiency is doubling year by year, meaning that the same facilities will deliver higher training efficiency and greater token output in the future.

Based on non-international financial reporting standards, third-quarter operating profit fell 6 percent to CNY68.1 billion from a year ago, while revenue rose 8 percent to CNY207.3 billion (USD31.1 billion), according to the earnings report. Tencent’s shares [HKG: 0700] finished 6.6 percent lower at HKD348.40 (USD44.41) each today, bringing the stock’s decline to 42 percent since the end of last year. The wider Hong Kong market lost almost 2 percent today.

Chip-Buying Curbs

Investment in AI infrastructure involves buying advanced-type chips, so Tencent’s management also addressed the impact of supply restrictions on the call.

The restrictions are a hurdle for all domestic players, and whether they rent or build computing power overseas, the advanced compute available has been reduced, Lau noted. Training will be affected, so Tencent’s next-generation model may take longer to release, he added.

But in the long run China’s supply chain is expected to mature and catch up, and on the AI inference side, since the models are highly efficient, the domestic supply chain is fully capable of supporting them, he pointed out. All Chinese players will likely eventually rely on domestically produced supply chains and chips, he stressed.

According to Mitchell, domestic chips can already run inference workloads efficiently on highly efficient models such as Tencent’s Hy4 flash. Over the past 12 months, inference efficiency has undergone a major shift, with token throughput on domestic chips far higher than anticipated a year ago, he said, noting that Tencent continues to add computing capacity through the Chinese supply chain.

 NOMURA CORPORATION 

 By Sherry Qin 

 Tencent Holdings' profit growth flatlined in the third quarter as surging investments in artificial intelligence eroded its bottom line. 

 Earnings have deteriorated in recent quarters as the Shenzhen-based company, among China's largest by market capitalization, stepped up its chip procurement this year to further advance its foundational models and various AI agent applications. 

 The videogame and social-media company said Wednesday that net profit edged 0.8% higher from a year earlier to 63.61 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.54 billion.  Revenue climbed by a smaller-than-expected 8% to 207.34 billion yuan. 

 The Chinese technology titan's capital expenditure jumped more than sixfold to 81.43 billion yuan in the third quarter, which kept it in negative free cash flow. 

 Ahead of the results, Macquarie analysts said it expected the company's prepayments for AI chips and components to support its AI initiatives to remain a near-term cost drag. 

 However, recent U.S. efforts to close loopholes and deny China access to advanced AI computing, including Nvidia's chips, could complicate Tencent's efforts to expand its AI chip inventory. 

 "Over time, this could constrain its ability to sustain the current pace of AI infrastructure investment and potentially drag down its pace of model development and rollout of new AI applications," Nomura analysts said in a note. 

 The company's bread-and-butter gaming business lost some momentum in the third quarter as revenue from domestic games rose 11% while international game revenue fell 9% due to a high base.

阿里巴巴集團首席財務官徐宏表示：「本季度，憑藉對 AI+雲增長及阿里電商集團盈利可持續性的戰略聚焦，我們的業務在收入和利潤兩方面均實現強勁增長。雲分部收入增長持續提速，高質量收益進一步驅動 EBITA利潤率升至 14.5%。電商分部 EBITA顯著增長，得益於即時零售單位經濟效益改善和遠場電商業務穩健增長。隨著 AI商業化不斷深入，我們會繼續審慎根據市場情况投入 AI建設，注重提升資本回報率，並致力於盡早實現自由現金流轉正。」

業績概要

截至 2026年 9月 30日止季度：

- 收入為人民幣 2,715.19億元（ 404.98億美元），同比增長10%。
- AI雲與算力服務收入同比增長 53%。外部客戶收入同比增長 64%，主要歸因於外部客戶經常性收入（不包括算力設備解決方案收入）增長 67%，這在很大程度上是由AI相關產品採用量的提升所帶動。
- 客戶管理收入同比下降 5%。若不考慮新營銷發展計劃所產生的視作收入沖減項影響，同口徑客戶管理收入同比增長將為1%。
- 經營利潤為人民幣 291.16億元（ 43.43億美元），同比增長 443%，主要是由於經調整 EBITA的增加。經調整 EBITA（一項非公認會計準則財務指標）同比增長 260%至人民幣 326.36億元（ 48.68億美元），主要歸因於淘寶閃購和雲業務的經營業績改善，以及多項業務運營效率的提升，部分被我們對科技投入的增加所抵銷。
- 歸屬於普通股股東的淨利潤為人民幣 645.35億元（ 96.26億美元）。 淨利潤為人民幣 644.20億元（ 96.08億美元），同比增長 213%，主要歸因於投資淨收益及經營利潤的增加。截至 2026年 9月 30日止季度，非公認會計準則淨利潤為人民幣 199.09億元（ 29.69億美元），相較 2025年同期的人民幣 103.52億元增長 92%。
- 攤薄每股美國存託股收益為人民幣 25.94元（ 3.87美元）。 攤薄每股收益為人民幣 3.24元（ 0.48美元或 3.78港元）。 非公認會計準則攤薄每股美國存託股收益為人民幣 8.10元（ 1.21美元），同比增長 86%。 非公認會計準則攤薄每股收益為人民幣 1.01元（ 0.15美元或 1.18港元），同比增長 86%。
- 經營活動產生的現金流量淨額為人民幣 156.90億元（ 23.40億美元），相較 2025年同期的人民幣 100.99億元增長 55%。 自由現金流（一項非公認會計準則財務流動性指標）為淨流出人民幣 344.72億元（ 51.42億美元）， 2025年同期為淨流出人民幣 218.40億元。自由現金流的下降主要歸因於我們的雲基礎設施支出增加，部分被淘寶閃購虧損減少以及我們雲服務的客戶預付款增加所抵銷。 於 2026年 9月 30日，我們的現金及其他流動投資 (1) 為人民幣 4,879.29億元（ 727.76億美元）。

截至 2026年 9月 30日止六個月：

- 收入為人民幣 5,404.72億元（ 806.13億美元），同比增長 9%。
- AI雲與算力服務收入同比增長 49%。外部客戶收入同比增長 56%，主要歸因於外部客戶經常性收入（不包括算力設備解決方案收入）增長 54%，這在很大程度上是由 AI相關產品採用量的提升所帶動。
- 客戶管理收入同比下降 6%。若不考慮新營銷發展計劃所產生的視作收入沖減項影響，同口徑客戶管理收入同比增長將為 1%。
- 經營利潤為人民幣 442.77億元（ 66.04億美元），同比增長 10%，主要是由於經調整 EBITA的增加所致，部分被商譽減值的增加以及本年度計提的準備金 (2) 所抵銷。經調整 EBITA（一項非公認會計準則財務指標）同比增長 25%至人民幣 599.65億元（ 89.44億美元），主要歸因於淘寶閃購和雲業務的經營業績改善，以及多項業務運營效率的提升，部分被我們對科技投入的增加所抵銷。
- 歸屬於普通股股東的淨利潤為人民幣 750.72億元（ 111.97億美元）。 淨利潤為人民幣 748.64億元（ 111.66億美元），同比增長 19%，主要歸因於投資淨收益及經營利潤的增加。 非公認會計準則淨利潤為人民幣 406.24億元（ 60.59億美元），相較 2025年同期的人民幣 438.62億元下降7%。
- 攤薄每股美國存託股收益為人民幣 29.91元（ 4.46美元）。 攤薄每股收益為人民幣 3.74元（ 0.56美元或 4.36港元）。 非公認會計準則攤薄每股美國存託股收益為人民幣 16.62元（ 2.48美元），同比下降 13%。 非公認會計準則攤薄每股收益為人民幣 2.08元（ 0.31美元或 2.42港元），同比下降 13%。
- 經營活動產生的現金流量淨額為人民幣 386.35億元（ 57.63億美元），相較 2025年同期的人民幣 307.71億元增長 26%。 自由現金流（一項非公認會計準則財務流動性指標）為淨流出人民幣 791.42億元（ 118.04億美元）， 2025年同期則為淨流出人民幣 406.55億元。 自由現金流的下降主要歸因於我們的雲基礎設施支出增加，部分被淘寶閃購虧損減少以及我們雲服務的客戶預付款增加所抵銷。 於 2026年 9月 30日，我們的現金及其他流動投資 (1) 為人民幣 4,879.29億元（ 727.76億美元）。

(2) 有關更多資料，請參見「截至 9月份止六個月其他財務業績」。

阿里巴巴電商集團

本季度，我們保持收入穩定，其中客戶管理收入同比下降5%；若不考慮營銷發展計劃所產生的視作收入沖減項的影響，同口徑客戶管理收入同比增長為1%。本季度，阿里巴巴電商集團經調整EBITA實現同比243%的增長，主要得益於中國即時零售業務大幅減虧。另外，中國電商業務經營利潤保持穩定、全球批發業務增長強勁，以及國際電商業務減虧。

我們持續推進戰略重點，釋放境內與跨境電商業務之間的顯著協同，並深化AI能力與電商平台相結合。近期進展包括整合國內與國際批發業務的管理，並於 10月推出一款由我們AI智能體能力驅動的面向商家的AI產品千問辦公電商版。

千問辦公電商版已整合至我們的一站式AI智能體平台千問辦公，旨在實現商家工作全流程的自動化，涵蓋店鋪運營、業務分析、營銷和客服。憑藉我們現有的商家工具，它可直接連接淘寶與天貓的數據，並將進一步支持其他平台的數據接入，實現更無縫的跨平台運營。此外，憑藉千問系列模型先進的多模態能力，我們能夠更好地理解複雜的消費者需求，並結合基於知識的推理提供更相關的產品推薦。這些能力的提升帶動泛知識查詢顯著增長，創造更多機會識別消費者潛在需求、促進商品發現，並推動銷售轉化。

中國即時零售業務方面，淘寶閃購在維持市場份額的同時，單位經濟效益環比持續改善。這反映筆單價提升，我們通過進一步改善訂單結構，拓展高筆單價的餐飲和非餐品類。另外，盒馬線上與線下渠道均保持強勁增長，得益於與淘寶閃購深化合作，以及拓展多業態門店網絡，為不同客群提供差異化的產品。

我們購買力最高的消費群體88VIP會員的數量持續同比雙位數增長，截至2026年9月30日約為6,600萬。新88VIP會員（定義為在過去一年內成為88VIP的用戶）在今年雙11大促期間ARPU同比上升顯著。面向我們最重要的客戶，我們將通過提升價值定位，繼續專注於提高 88VIP會員的規模和留存。

閑魚是中國領先的C2C社區和閒置物品交易平台。閑魚通過提供各種AI驅動的能力，包括智能定價、生成產品描述、目標買家識別，以及幫賣託管，幫助個人用戶和小商家實現更便捷的買賣交易。本季度，閑魚業務持續強勁增長，日活躍用戶同比增長 23%，支付訂單同比增長29%。

AI雲與算力服務

截至2026年9月30日止季度，AI雲與算力服務收入為人民幣609.73億元（90.94億美元），同比增長53%。外部客戶收入同比增長加速至64%。外部客戶經常性收入（剔除算力設備解決方案收入），同比增長亦達到67%。其中，AI相關產品收入保持強勁勢頭，達179.18億元人民幣（26.73億美元），實現連續第十三個季度的三位數同比增長。強勁增長反映了市場對我們AI+雲服務的廣泛需求，除AI實驗室的訓練和推理工作負載外，互聯網、汽車、具身智能、金融服務及生物科技等行業客戶亦迅速擴大使用我們雲服務的規模，支持其創新和業務增長。

阿里雲持續增強行業領先的全棧AI能力，並在9月的雲棲大會上公佈涵蓋自研芯片、超節點架構、智能體原生雲基礎設施、AI模型和智能體的全面升級。我們協同設計的全棧能力提升加速企業使用，以及與核心業務工作流程更深度的融合，讓我們能夠把握各行業日益多元化需求帶來的商業化機遇。

我們賦能企業級AI落地的能力得到高度認可——Gartner®發佈《2026年戰略雲平台服務魔力象限™》，全面評估雲服務商在企業雲全生命週期的支持能力，阿里雲獲評為最高象限的領導者，成為亞太地區首家且唯一獲此殊榮的服務商。

芯片設計 — 平頭哥半導體（「平頭哥」）

平頭哥通過快速升級其自研芯片和軟件產品組合，進一步夯實支撐我們AI能力的基礎設施底座。

在9月的雲棲大會上，我們發佈下一代訓推一體AI芯片——真武V900，計劃於2027年第一季度上市。真武V900基於我們自研的並行計算架構，相較上一代真武M890實現顯著的性能提升。我們還開源了真武芯片的軟件棧——平頭哥SAIL，以簡化應用遷移、推廣開發者使用，並加強與主流AI框架的兼容性。

此外，我們於8月推出真武M890超節點實例，標誌著中國首個能支持超過兩萬億參數模型推理的超節點架構問世。在雲棲大會上，我們還展示了下一代超節點產品，該產品集成真武V900與其他自研的互聯、網絡及存儲芯片，計劃於2027年第一季度推出。

我們持續升級全棧模型產品組合，聚焦於基礎模型，同時提升視頻、語音、圖像及音樂等模型能力，展現我們行業領先與快速迭代的能力。

近期，我們發佈了Qwen4-Max，該模型基於全新的混合專家架構，擁有2.4萬億主幹參數，並具備原生視覺能力。Qwen4-Max提升了生產力及Token使用效率，在製造業、遊戲開發、醫療及前沿科學研究等領域具備更強的長週期任務執行能力。

千問辦公

我們的智能體平台千問辦公持續在各大行業獲得廣泛採用，這得益於其企業級能力的不斷增強。在9月的雲棲大會上，我們推出企業上下文，該解決方案能持續整理並更新企業文檔、會議紀要及內部溝通中的企業信息與知識。它讓AI智能體基於企業信息，組織知識和工作流程執行任務。

# Citi Just Cut Its Alibaba Target to $160. Could the Stock Really Climb 97%?
Gian Estrada Sun, November 22, 2026 at 5:57 AM EST 4 min read
## Trading disclosure

Citi Just Cut Its Alibaba Target to $160. Could the Stock Really Climb 97%? ©@Stefanut Sava's Images via Canva ## Key Takeaways
* Citi cut its Alibaba price target to $160 from $193 on Nov. 20 and kept its Buy rating, a day after a September-quarter report in which adjusted earnings missed estimates.
* At $160, Alibaba would trade at about 18x fiscal 2028 earnings estimates, against 10x forward earnings today and a five-year average of 13x.
* CEO Eddie Wu says new U.S. chip rules could slow cloud growth to 30% to 45% next fiscal year. Rival Baidu's AI cloud revenue grew 94% last quarter.
* With earnings estimates still slipping, Citi's target looks too optimistic, and the December-quarter report is the next test.
**Alibaba** (**BABA:NYSE**) fell 2.7% to $81.08 on Friday, Nov. 20, its lowest close in a year and 54% below its January high. The same day, Citi's Alicia Yap kept her Buy rating and cut her price target to $160 from $193, still 97% above the stock.
Citi called Alibaba's lower cloud outlook "pragmatic" given new export rules and blamed the cut on lower valuations across the sector, according to TheFly. Three days before Alibaba reported, **Baidu** (**BIDU:NASDAQ**) said its AI Cloud Infra revenue grew 94% to RMB 8.2 billion (about $1.2 billion), about one-seventh the size of Alibaba's cloud business.
## Alibaba Is Paying for the AI Build-Out
Capex rose to RMB 126.1 billion (about $18.8 billion) in fiscal 2026, the year ended March 2026, from RMB 86.0 billion (about $12.8 billion) a year earlier. Free cash flow turned to a RMB 46.6 billion (about $7.0 billion) outflow, and in August Alibaba sold HK$80 billion (about $10.2 billion) of new shares.
In the Nov. 19 report, adjusted earnings rose 86% to RMB 8.10 (about $1.21) per ADS but missed estimates, and free cash flow was an outflow of RMB 34.5 billion (about $5.1 billion). Cloud revenue grew 53%. On the call, Wu pointed to new U.S. rules that cut into the offshore chips Alibaba rents and said Alibaba might target cloud growth of 30% to 45% in the fiscal year ending March 2028, rebounding to 50% or more in calendar 2028.
Barclays, Jefferies and Baird cut their targets too, Baird to $128 from $160, but all three kept bullish ratings.
## Does Alibaba's $160 Add Up?
Analysts expect earnings to climb back to about fiscal 2024's level by fiscal 2028.
BABA Normalized EPS, Actual and Estimates (RMB per ADS): FY2024-FY2028 (TIKR)
Those estimates are slipping, though. The fiscal 2027 consensus has fallen to RMB 43.47 (about $6.48) per ADS from RMB 44.45 (about $6.63) in late October, and fiscal 2028's to RMB 61.03 (about $9.10) from RMB 62.05 (about $9.26).

The stock trades at 10x forward earnings, below its five-year average of 13x. Baidu traded at 17x on Nov. 19.
BABA Stock NTM P/E: 5-Year (TIKR)
Citi's $160 works out to about 18x fiscal 2028 estimates. A year from now, nearly two-thirds of the forward window falls in fiscal 2029, but it would take earnings growth of about 57% that year to bring $160 down to the 13x average.
## Too Big an Ask for Alibaba Right Now
Alibaba also faces a new securities class action tied to its export-control troubles.
At 10x, the stock looks cheap enough to bounce. But short of that 57% jump, $160 needs the stock to re-rate above its five-year average while estimates drift lower. I think Citi's target is too optimistic for the next 12 months.
The December-quarter report, due early next year, is the next test. If cloud growth stays near this quarter's 53% and the free cash flow outflow comes in smaller than RMB 34.5 billion, $160 would look a lot more reasonable.

# 阿里雲AI業務勝預期 瑞銀滙豐予買入花旗下調目標價 

 財經 發佈 20.11.2026 09:30 最後更新 20.11.2026 09:30 

 來源：阿里巴巴facebook 

阿里巴巴(09988.HK)第2財季AI雲與算力服務收入增長53%勝市場預期，帶動整體經調整EBITA大幅增長。瑞銀及滙豐均維持「買入」評級，認為雲業務收入加速及利潤率改善，有助支持集團長線AI發展；不過，花旗下調阿里巴巴目標價，反映市場關注明年雲收入增速放緩及算力出口限制的影響。

滙豐指出，業績勝預期主要由於雲業務利潤率優於預期。AI及雲計算服務收入上季按年增長53%至610億元，較滙豐及市場預期高13%。運算設備解決方案收入首次披露，達100億元，按年增長55%。

不過，集團上季資本開支按年增加60%至505億元，反映AI基礎設施投入持續擴張。瑞銀指出，市場關注美國收緊對中國企業遠端使用先進晶片的限制後，阿里雲明年增長預期已有所下調，投資者亦關注公司能否維持AI雲業務增長及資本開支節奏。

花旗表示，阿里重申2030年及2031年的雲業務目標，顯示短期政策逆風不改長期需求機遇。即使行業整體估值下調，但阿里憑藉自研晶片的AI全棧技術，在應對算力供應限制方面處於相對有利位置。

即時零售方面，收入增速明顯放緩。瑞銀估計，這項業務上季虧損約90億元，與對上一季相若，主要因客單價上升、競爭趨於理性，以及納入盈利的盒馬業務，令單位經濟效益改善。瑞銀認為，管理層的策略及減虧速度，是市場其後關注重點。

花旗下調阿里目標價，ADR160美元、港股159港元，主要因公司預計明年雲服務收入增速將由目前的53%放緩至30%至45%，而2028年才有望重回50%以上。花旗認為，指引反映阿里對算力出口限制不斷演變的務實應對，但長期AI發展雄心不變。

# Alibaba HK shares rise as Q2 topline beat invites some bargain buying

Author Ambar Warrick

Published Nov 19, 2026, 10:37 PM

Alibaba HK shares rise as Q2 topline beat invites some bargain buying

© Reuters.

Investing.com-- Alibaba’s Hong Kong shares rose on Friday as stronger-than-expected second fiscal quarter revenue invited some bargain buying into the battered Chinese tech giant.

Alibaba Group (HK: 9988) rose as much as 2.7% to HK$83.15, outpacing an over 2% slump in the Hang Seng index. The stock rose after hitting a near two-year low on Thursday. 

The e-commerce giant on Thursday reported stronger-than-expected revenue for the quarter to September 30, aided by improving returns from artificial intelligence cloud and computing services. 

Adjusted profit also rose sharply in the quarter, aided by some improvement in margins and narrower losses in the company’s growing quick-commerce business. 

The earnings print helped restore some confidence in Alibaba, whose shares were battered by mounting concerns over the company’s access to offshore advanced AI chips, which was effectively cut off by new U.S. restrictions this week. 

Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the company’s 2030 targets of $100 billion in external cloud revenue and 20% EBITDA margin remained on track, despite the new restrictions.

The company is also facing a shareholder class action lawsuit over allegations that it hid its ties to a suspected Chinese spy who was involved with Nvidia. 

Alibaba’s gains on Friday came amid a broader rout in tech and AI stocks, amid mounting questions over the long-term returns from the technology.

Frontier AI lab Anthropic’s bumper market debut on Thursday did little to lift sentiment towards the sector.

Alibaba, along with peers Baidu and Tencent, is regarded as being at the forefront of China’s AI development efforts. But this has left the stock exposed to a deep rout in AI valuations since October.

# Alibaba Gains 3.5% on Cloud Jump as Hong Kong Tech Sinks 3.8%

## The company's September-quarter results showed strong cloud and e-commerce earnings growth, although non-GAAP net income missed market expectations and capital spending increased.

 By Gary zhou Published 21 November 2026, 3:52 AM HKT

 Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images 

Alibaba Group (9988.HK) closed 3.48% higher in Hong Kong on Friday, Nov. 20, the day after it reported September-quarter results. On the same day the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 3.78% to 3,511.14, its eighth losing session in a row.

The rest of the sector went the other way. NetEase fell more than 17% and Kuaishou more than 11%, and chip and optical-communications stocks also fell. The Hang Seng Index lost 1.89% to 22,410.80. Alibaba shares worth HK$12.19 billion changed hands. Over the week, the tech index fell 7.92% and the benchmark 5.19%.

The cloud business drove the gain. Revenue from AI Cloud and Compute Services rose 53% from a year earlier to RMB60.97 billion (US$9.09 billion), Alibaba said in its results release. Revenue from external customers grew 64%. Recurring revenue from those customers, which excludes compute equipment sales, rose 67%. Group revenue rose 10% to RMB271.52 billion.

The profit lines told different stories. Adjusted EBITA rose 260% to RMB32.64 billion. Much of that came from the e-commerce group, where adjusted EBITA more than tripled to RMB38.85 billion as Taobao Instant Commerce improved its unit economics. Net income rose 213% to RMB64.42 billion, which the company put down mainly to higher net investment income and higher operating income. Non-GAAP net income, which strips out investment gains, rose a more modest 92% to RMB19.91 billion.

Non-GAAP net income was the one figure that missed. UBS said the market had expected about RMB26 billion and that the shortfall probably reflected a one-off tax item. It also said adjusted EBITA beat expectations by 16%.

"This quarter, our business delivered strong growth in both revenue and earnings," Chief Financial Officer Toby Xu said in the release.

Capital spending rose too. It climbed 60% to RMB50.48 billion in the quarter, and free cash flow was an outflow of RMB34.47 billion, compared with an outflow of RMB21.84 billion a year earlier. The quarter's financing included the HK$80 billion share placement Alibaba completed in late August, the largest follow-on offering ever by a Hong Kong-listed company. Alibaba ended September with RMB487.93 billion in cash and liquid investments.

# Meituan's Third-Quarter Profit Likely to Decline Sequentially -- Earnings Preview

Nov. 25, 2026, 2:16 a.m. ET

By Tracy Qu

Meituan is scheduled to report results for the third quarter on Friday. Here's what you need to know:

NET PROFIT FORECAST: The Chinese food-delivery company is expected to report a net profit of 354.7 million yuan, equivalent to $53.2 million, according to the consensus estimate of 10 analysts compiled by FactSet. That compares with an 18.63 billion yuan net loss reported in the year-earlier period and 2.15 billion yuan net profit in the second quarter.

REVENUE FORECAST: Revenue is expected at 113.56 billion yuan, up from 95.49 billion yuan a year earlier.

Its Hong Kong-listed shares were 4.7% higher in the three months ended September amid broader weakness among tech stocks.

WHAT TO WATCH:

--NEAR-TERM PRESSURE: Meituan likely faced seasonal pressure in 3Q with food delivery's profitability likely weakening from 2Q, said UOB Kay Hian's Julia Pan in a note. Meanwhile, in-store, hotel and travel segment margins likely normalized in 3Q amid softer travel demand and higher marketing expenses, she added.

--EARNINGS: Meituan's recovery trajectory is still on track but could be slower than previously anticipated, according to Fitch Ratings. The ratings firm expects Meituan's Ebitda to remain under pressure in 2026, while the Chinese delivery platform's free cash flow is likely to only turn positive in 2027. This is due to intense competition in the country's food delivery sector, with high subsidy spending weakening near-term earnings visibility. # Xiaomi profit falls as China auto downturn weighs, eyes Europe car market 

By

Published Nov 24, 2026, 04:47 AM

Updated Nov 24, 2026, 07:36 AM

© Reuters.

By Ju-min Park

BEIJING, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Chinese electric-vehicle and smartphone maker Xiaomi Corp reported a 57% fall in third-quarter net profit on Tuesday, missing analyst estimates, as a downturn in China’s auto market and higher component costs weighed on earnings.

The Hong Kong-listed company also said it planned to enter Germany’s car market in the second half of 2027 as part of its overseas expansion.

Xiaomi reported adjusted net profit of 4.9 billion yuan ($735.7 million) for July to September, below analysts’ average estimate of 5.2 billion yuan, according to LSEG data.

Its shares closed down 3.7% at HK$26.5.

XIAOMI EYES GERMANY ENTRY AS DOMESTIC CAR MARKET WEAKENS

Xiaomi’s New Energy Vehicle (NEV), AI and other new initiatives segment swung to an operating loss of 3.4 billion yuan in the quarter. Revenue from its NEV business fell 19.9% to 22.7 billion yuan as vehicle deliveries declined.

The company delivered 100,975 vehicles during the quarter, down 7.2 % from a year ago based on its earlier statements.

Overall retail sales in China’s passenger vehicle market fell 24% year-on-year, Xiaomi said, citing industry data.

On its post-earnings call, Xiaomi said the domestic auto market downturn was creating "huge pressure for everyone".

It also highlighted rising costs and inventories as challenges for its automotive business.

However, Xiaomi said it planned to enter the German car market in the second half of 2027 and was conducting vehicle testing in several European countries.

Analysts have flagged intensifying price competition and a weakening domestic auto market as risks to Xiaomi’s automotive business. Sales of its recently launched SkyNomad SUV series have only partly offset lower shipments of older models, they said.

PREMIUM PHONE PUSH TO OFFSET MEMORY COSTS

The world’s third-largest smartphone maker after Samsung and Apple said total third-quarter revenue fell 5.2% to 107.2 billion yuan, while smartphone revenue slipped 0.8%.

Its smartphone gross margin fell to 9.2% from 11.1% a year earlier due to continuing high memory costs.

However, Xiaomi said average smartphone selling prices rose 10% from the previous quarter as it shifted its product mix towards higher-end models.

Research firm Counterpoint said Xiaomi experienced a "significant shipment decline" of more than 30% in the third quarter, with its market share falling to 12%.

The company has cut exposure to lower-priced segments and non-core overseas markets, Counterpoint said.

Xiaomi launched a new flagship foldable smartphone in September as it sought to compete more directly with Apple, which also released its first foldable device that month. 

AI, ROBOTICS INVESTMENT CONTINUES

Xiaomi said it would continue investing in AI, self-developed chips and robotics despite near-term pressure on profitability.

The company said its humanoid robots had completed eight hours of continuous operation at a sorting station on its car production lines, including autonomous recharging.

Xiaomi said it was also testing its robots in home-like conditions.

According to Zhitong Finance APP, BofA Securities issued a research report stating that it slightly raised its adjusted earnings forecast for XIAOMI-W (01810) for 2026 by 2% to reflect performance and lower R&D assumptions. It maintained a sum-of-the-parts based price target of HK$34 and reiterated its "Buy" rating. The company's adjusted profit for the third quarter was RMB 4.9 billion, broadly in line with expectations; revenue amounted to RMB 107 billion, 5% higher than the firm's expectation and in line with market consensus. The gross margin was 20.2%, an increase of 0.3 percentage points quarter-on-quarter, exceeding the firm's and market expectations by 0.4 and 0.2 percentage points, respectively, indicating stabilizing profit margins.

The firm pointed out that smartphone revenue and gross margin in the third quarter outperformed expectations, benefiting from strong Average Selling Price and product mix. Management expects NAND prices to largely stabilize, while DRAM prices are projected to continue rising until the first half of 2027. Smartphone Average Selling Price is expected to continue growing through 2027, and management expressed confidence in maintaining healthy gross margins.

Regarding IoT, management emphasized that the worst period has passed. Revenue from TVs and home appliances turned positive year-on-year in the third quarter, with robust contributions from overseas markets. Overseas markets accounted for 30% of IoT revenue in the third quarter, and this proportion is expected to continue growing with channel and product mix expansion.

In the electric vehicle segment, the firm noted that SkyNomad helps drive cross-selling of the SU7 and YU7 models. Deliveries are expected to rebound significantly quarter-on-quarter in the fourth quarter, with October deliveries exceeding 50,000 units. Overseas EV expansion is proceeding as planned; the company has signed agreements with eight major channel dealers in Germany and has begun expanding into right-hand drive markets.

AI-related R&D expenses exceeded RMB 2.8 billion in the third quarter, accounting for over 30% of total R&D spending. The deployment of large language models has extended from smartphones to electric vehicles, which may aid long-term monetization.

# Xiaomi profit misses Q3 forecasts as EV and smartphone sales shrink

Author Vahid Karaahmetovic

Published Nov 24, 2026, 05:50 AM

© Reuters.

1810+0.23%

Investing.com -- Xiaomi’s third-quarter net profit fell 57% and missed analyst estimates, as sales declined in both its electric-vehicle and smartphone businesses.

The Hong Kong-listed company posted adjusted net profit of 4.9 billion yuan for July through September. That fell short of the 5.2 billion yuan average estimate in LSEG data.

Revenue dropped 5.2% from a year earlier to 107.2 billion yuan. Smartphones, its biggest business, brought in 46.0 billion yuan, down 0.8%. 

Smartphone shipments slid 20% to 30.7 million units, which Xiaomi attributed partly to fewer low-end handsets sold worldwide. The average selling price hit a record 1,486 yuan, up 40% from a year earlier.

Margins on phones narrowed to 9.2% from 11.1%, with Xiaomi pointing to persistently high memory costs.

According to Counterpoint Research, Xiaomi has pulled back from lower-priced segments and non-core overseas markets as it pushes toward premium devices. In September, the company launched a flagship foldable phone to compete more directly with Apple, which unveiled its first foldable.

Electric-vehicle revenue fell 19.9% to 22.7 billion yuan, which Xiaomi blamed on lower deliveries. Its unit covering EVs, artificial intelligence and other new initiatives lost 3.4 billion yuan at the operating level.

Sales of Internet-of-Things and lifestyle products, including washing machines and vacuum cleaners, slipped 1.45% to 27.15 billion yuan. Weaker demand for some lifestyle products outweighed gains in laptops, tablets and large smart appliances.

Rising component costs and softer sales cut the overall gross margin to 20.2% from 22.9% a year earlier.

# 小米：坑是爬出来了，但未来在哪里？

Xiaomi Corp. (1810.HK) released its Q3 2026 results (quarter ended Sep 2026) after the Hong Kong close on Nov 24 Beijing time. Key highlights follow: $小米集团-W(01810.HK)

1. Overall results: revenue was RMB 107.2bn, down 5.2% YoY, in line with the street's RMB 106.5bn.

Legacy biz (Smartphones × AIoT) delivered RMB 83.4bn, down 0.9% YoY. NEV and AI-related innovation revenue was RMB 23.9bn, down 17.7% YoY, below the RMB 25.8bn consensus, mainly on lower auto volume and ASP.

Group GPM was 20.2%, up 40bps QoQ, broadly in line with the 20.0% street est.

QoQ improvement was led by legacy biz: smartphone GPM improved from 8.5% to 9.2% and IoT GPM from 20.1% to 21.7%. NEV and AI innovation GPM was flat at 19.2%.

2. Autos: segment revenue was RMB 23.9bn (NEV revenue RMB 22.7bn), below the RMB 25.8bn consensus.

With the range-extended 'Pengcheng' added, the segment was renamed from 'Smart EV and AI Innovation' to 'NEV and AI Innovation' starting this quarter. Deliveries were 101k units, down 7.2% YoY, with the Pengcheng series (launched on Sep 7) contributing over 10k units.

ASP was ~RMB 225k, down about 2% QoQ, below the RMB 237k street est, and ASP pressure was the key driver of the revenue miss. Q3 deliveries were still dominated by the new-gen SU7 and YU7, while the higher-priced Pengcheng N90 only started deliveries in Sep, with ASP uplift to show in Q4.

Auto segment GPM (NEV and AI innovation) was 19.2%, flat QoQ, slightly below the 19.4% street est. The company cited a lower mix of SU7 Ultra deliveries, higher core component prices, and rising AI costs.

Management added that post-Pengcheng launch, Xiaomi Auto maintained a 'high and healthy' margin level and remains confident in sustaining auto GPM.

3. Smartphones: RMB 45.6bn, down 0.8% YoY, up 8.2% QoQ and ahead of the RMB 43.0bn street est.

Shipments were 30.7mn units, broadly in line. ASP was RMB 1,486, up 39.8% YoY, the key beat driver, reflecting the ongoing 'control volume, protect price' strategy.

By market, China shipments were ~8mn units, down ~20% YoY, with a 13.8% share. Overseas shipments were ~22.7mn units, down ~32% YoY, with overseas share down to 11.5% YoY, as the deliberate pullback in low-end models overseas drove the shipment decline.

ASP kept rising, driven by two factors: 1) under memory tightness, the company prioritized allocation to higher-priced models. 2) cost pressure prompted price hikes across the portfolio.

Smartphone GPM was 9.2%, up 70bps QoQ, above the 8.6% street est. Management attributed the QoQ uplift to a better mix led by domestic premium launches, partially offset by core component price increases.

For 9M26, smartphone GPM averaged ~9.3%, aligning with the prior '9%+' full-year guidance. Management expects memory costs to remain relatively high in 2027, making further ASP uplift vs. 2026 a 'given', and is confident in sustaining healthy smartphone margins.

4. IoT: RMB 27.2bn, down 1.4% YoY, slightly below the RMB 27.6bn street est. As last year's high base from state subsidies was digested, YoY declines narrowed markedly vs. the prior three quarters (~20%).

IoT GPM was 21.7%, up 160bps QoQ and above the 21.2% street est. The QoQ uplift came from higher margins in ACs and laptops, as well as higher margins and mix for overseas wearables.

To meet the prior full-year guidance of -5% to -10%, Q4 YoY growth needs to be about 13%–38%. Management said IoT has 'exited the difficult phase and entered a steady growth phase'.

5. Internet services were RMB 9.5bn, up 0.7% YoY, in line with the RMB 9.4bn street est. Internet GPM was 73.8%, down 300bps QoQ, mainly due to a lower contribution from pre-installs, which dragged ad margins as smartphone shipments declined and flowed through to high-margin pre-install revenue.

By region: overseas internet revenue was RMB 3.2bn, down ~1.5% YoY. Domestic internet revenue was ~RMB 6.2bn, up ~2% YoY.

Domestic MAU reached 199mn, up 6.4% YoY. Overseas MAU was ~573mn, up 3.3% YoY.

6. Profit: core profit RMB 2.1bn, adj. NP RMB 4.9bn. On Dolphin Research definition (GP minus S&M, G&A and R&D), core profit was RMB 2.14bn, down 68% YoY, with a 2.0% core margin.

By segment, legacy core profit was ~RMB 5.5bn, down ~8% YoY. NEV and AI innovation posted a RMB 3.4bn loss, widening by ~RMB 0.8bn QoQ.
